diagnosis.summary: A traffic spike is affecting product-service, cart-service, and order-service simultaneously. Request rates have risen roughly 3x across all three services compared to baseline. No errors or meaningful latency increases are present at this time.
diagnosis.root_cause: A coordinated surge in incoming traffic across all three services is the most likely root cause, with product-service absorbing the largest absolute load increase and all services remaining healthy so far.
evidence: product-service request rate rose from 15.0 rps to 45.1 rps, a 3x increase.
cart-service request rate rose from 2.0 rps to 6.0 rps, also a 3x increase.
order-service request rate rose from 2.9 rps to 8.8 rps, approximately a 3x increase.
product-service p95 latency increased modestly from 24 ms to 31 ms, and order-service p95 latency moved from 58 ms to 61 ms, both well within normal range.
product-service error_rate_5xx remains at 0.0 with no errors observed during the spike.
recommended_actions: Monitor DynamoDB consumed capacity and throttle metrics on all three tables as load continues, since a 3x traffic increase may push provisioned capacity limits.
Watch Lambda concurrency and cold_start_count across product-service, cart-service, and order-service for signs of scaling pressure.
Check order-service dependency calls to payment-service for rising latency or error counts as order traffic has tripled.
If the spike is sustained, consider increasing DynamoDB provisioned or auto-scaling capacity on the product-service, cart-service, and order-service tables proactively.
